cleaned.ingredients:
Ladies finger – 250 g (15–18 pods), cut into 1-inch pieces
Onion – 1 medium, finely chopped
Tomato – 1 medium, chopped
Green chili – 1–2, slit
Curry leaves – 8–10
Turmeric powder – ¼ tsp
Coriander powder – 1½ tsp
Tamarind pulp- 3 tbsp
Dates paste- 2 tbsp
Red chili powder – ½ tsp (adjust to spice)
Salt – to taste
Water – 1 cup (adjust for gravy consistency)
Optional tempering :
Mustard seeds – ½ tsp
Curry leaves – few
cleaned.steps:
Heat a pan, add in the mustard seeds, once splutter add the curry leaves and asafoetida.
In a pan, add the chopped onion and a splash of water and cook till soft and translucent. Add the chopped ladies finger and saute on on low flame for about 5–6 minutes until the stickiness reduces and set aside.
Then add tomato, green chilli, curry leaves, turmeric, coriander, and chilli powder. Cover and cook for 5–7 minutes till the tomato softens.
Add the tamarind pulp, date paste and 1-1.5 cup water, mix well, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the salt, and cook for 8–10 minutes on medium-low flame until the curry thickens and the flavours blend.
Turn off the heat and add a few fresh curry leaves or a squeeze of lime for freshness before serving.
Tastes best with steamed red rice, millet rice, or soft dosas.

1 cup millet flour (you can use any variety of millet flour such as pearl millet, jowar, finger millet, or sorghum millet)
1/4 teaspoon salt
Warm water, as needed
Extra millet flour for dusting
cleaned.steps:
In a mixing bowl, combine millet flour and salt.
Gradually add warm water, a little at a time, and knead the dough until it comes together and is smooth and pliable. The amount of water needed may vary depending on the flour, so add it gradually until you achieve the right consistency.
Divide the dough into 4 equal portions and roll each portion into a smooth ball.
Heat a tawa (flat griddle) or a non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Take one portion of the dough and flatten it slightly between your palms to form a small disc.
Dust the disc with millet flour to prevent sticking and roll it out into a thin round roti using a rolling pin. If the roti sticks to the rolling pin or surface, dust it with more millet flour.
Carefully transfer the rolled-out roti onto the hot tawa or skillet.
Cook the roti for about 1-2 minutes on one side until small bubbles start to form.
Flip the roti and cook for another 1-2 minutes on the other side until it puffs up slightly and brown spots appear.

3-4 pods garlic, finely chopped

Spices : 1/2 tsp cumin powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1/2 tsp red chilli powder, 1/4 tsp turmeric powder, 2 tsp curry powder

cleaned.steps:
Rinse red lentils thoroughly and set aside.
To a pre-heated pan, add in oil, garlic, ginger and green chilli.
Saute till the garlic turns slightly golden. Add in all the spices.
Spice powders tend to burn quickly so turn down the heat and stir continuously for a minute.
Add in the tomato pure, washed lentils and broth. Mix everything together.
Cover the pan with a lid and let the lentils cook for 25 minutes.
Once done do a taste test. Add in 1/4 cup plant milk to balance the spice if required.
Transfer the red lentils to a serving bowl and sprinkle finely chopped coriander leaves and lemon juice. Serve red lentils over a bed of brown or red rice or with serve with hot pulkhas

cleaned.steps:
Pre-heat a pan, saute onions, garlic and green chillies. Once the onions are translucent, add in blended tomatoes, spice powders and methi leaves. Saute them for a minute.
Add washed lentils and 2 cups water to the pan and cook for 15-20 minutes on medium flame.
Parallely, in a fresh pan, add in brinjal cubes and saute till they are soft. Once tender, add in cumin seeds and cardamom powder. Use water as needed.
Transfer the tender brinjal to the lentil pan and stir well to combine.
Add in salt as required and continue to cook for 5 more minutes.
Add in more water if required.
Do a taste test and adjust the spices and salt accordingly.
Serve this brinjal lentil curry with quinoa or red rice or with hot chapati(s)

cleaned.ingredients:
2 tablespoons chia seeds
1/2 cup unsweetened almond milk
1/4 teaspoon vanilla extract
1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1/2 banana, sliced
1/2 apple, chopped
1 tablespoon nut butter of your choice (e.g. almond butter, cashew butter, etc.)
1 tablespoon chopped nuts
(e.g. walnuts, pecans, almonds, etc.)
cleaned.steps:
In a mixing bowl, combine the chia seeds, almond milk, vanilla extract, and cinnamon powder. Mix well until the chia seeds are evenly distributed.
Let the mixture sit for about 10 minutes to allow the chia seeds to absorb the liquid and form a pudding-like texture.
While waiting, chop the fruits and prepare the nut butter and chopped nuts.
Once the chia pudding has set, start layering the parfait. Begin with a layer of chia pudding at the bottom of a glass or jar, then add a layer of sliced bananas, followed by a layer of chopped apples.
Next, add a dollop of nut butter on top of the fruit layer, then sprinkle some chopped nuts over it.
Repeat the layering process until you reach the top of the glass or jar, making sure to end with a layer of chopped nuts on top.
Sprinkle some extra cinnamon powder on top if desired.
Serve immediately or refrigerate until ready to serve.
